findings.summary: Fixed 32-row kernels now execute throughout the decoder. NACA OCR is 82.7% of a 2.561 s call; narrow projection kernels often launch only 8–16 blocks across 58 SMs.
observations: The complete five-PDF evaluator passed all 30 calls and 2,790 raw EOS checks. Versus fresh default tiles, p50 speedup improved 13.7%, p95 improved 22.0%, and throughput improved 18.4%. All five per-PDF medians improved.

This separate diagnostic passed three ordinary calls and its full instrumented output check. NACA median is 2.561 s, OCR 2.115 s and embedding 0.286 s. Mean stage shares are 82.7% OCR and 11.3% embedding.

Each GPU records 2,336 persistent matmul launches with 128-thread blocks: 32 engine iterations times 73 decoder projections per iteration (18 layers times 4 projections, plus the vocabulary head). The previous bucketed attempt changed only 32 head launches per GPU. Compiled graph code also now uses 32-row divisions.

The recorded decoder grids frequently contain 16 blocks, and GPU 3 also records 180 launches with 8 blocks. A block executes on one SM, so these kernels can use at most 16 or 8 of the 58 L4 SMs simultaneously. This is a specific launch-capacity limit, not a claim about whole-GPU or memory-bandwidth saturation.

The inherited 128-column tile creates these small grids for 1,024-wide attention-output and down projections. Reducing the column width increases independent blocks while leaving the K=64 reduction unchanged. Actual performance and bitwise equivalence must be screened.

A separate fixed-row screen passed 120 bitwise cases at decode and prefill sizes. 16 rows give small mixed decode gains and substantial prefill penalties; 64 improves some prefill cases but often slows decode. Keep 32 rows while testing column width.

The bounded trace includes vision prefill. Kernel-duration sums do not establish whole-call stage shares or isolate hardware peak throughput. GPU activity samples are sparse on this short document; raw launch grids are stronger evidence for this particular limitation.
findings.next_step: Screen narrower column tiles for the small decoder projections, checking every output bit and both decode/prefill costs. Then evaluate a promising shape-specific configuration against fixed 32-row/128-column control on all five frozen PDFs.
findings.optimization: Keep batch invariance, K=64 reduction, model precision, four GPUs, routing, proposal depth, embeddings and frozen references fixed; choose columns per model matrix shape rather than per PDF.
